examples.name: Sample — waw
paragraphs: Five boxed ACA panels laid out in two rows, each with its own title band and its own full header stack. The dark band across the top of each panel shares its frame, so it is the first row of that panel's table. Carrier Cata- / strophic is one wrapped label; the lower panels print Cata-strophic with the hyphen mid-line, so the hyphen is part of the printed word and is kept.

examples.name: Counter-sample — figure-cards-p6
paragraphs: The Figure 5 boxed panels look like side-by-side mini-tables but are image-plus-caption cards, not tabular data: they are rendered as the figure's content in reading order. The only table on the page is Table 3, whose bold Total row closes it.

examples.name: Sample — a two-sided balance sheet in one frame
paragraphs: Assets down the left, liabilities and equity down the middle, an income statement on the right, all inside one ruled box under two title bands. These are different schemas, not consecutive ranges of a repeated schema. Repeated-schema continuations follow Column Continuation§9.2.2 even inside one enclosing frame. Row n on the left has nothing to do with row n in the middle, and yet this is one table, row n across all blocks — the frame is one grid and is transcribed as the grid it prints. The side-by-side rule above is for boxes with their own frames.
